faults.quote: What's missing from it, and which branch would you check first, and why?
faults.why: This stacks three questions in one tail.

faults.quote: New customers per month were 500 Pro in 2024, before Starter launched, and 350 Pro plus 1,000 Starter — 1,350 in total — from January 2025 to June 2026.
faults.why: The candidate asked how Pro volume moved month to month. Only period averages were given, with no 'I don't have a month-by-month cut'.

faults.quote: I can share plan economics: monthly price and cost to serve for Pro and Starter if you'd like.
faults.why: The candidate had not asked for price or cost to serve, so this offers gated data unprompted.

faults.quote: Most upgrades are between months 3 and 9, usually when the business hires its first employee; very few are after month 12.
faults.why: The candidate asked whether upgraders are mainly the 150 would-be Pro buyers. Upgrade timing doesn't answer that, and no 'I don't have that split' was given.

faults.quote: As the exhibit shows: Of the 3,000 Starter customers who signed up in January–March 2025, 94% were still on Starter after month 1
faults.why: This repeats the Exhibit 2 data already on screen as part of the answer to an ask it doesn't address.

faults.quote: Which customers did you count as having left in that 40% still on Starter at month 12?
faults.why: In t19 the candidate had already said the 40% excludes upgraders and that 7% bundles cancellers and upgraders. This re-asks the same point with no new angle.

faults.quote: You had "$920" as the net value of a Starter sign-up. What were the steps in that calculation, and in particular what lifetime and cancellation rate sit behind the Starter margin piece?
faults.why: This is the third probe (after t18 and t22, then t28) on the misread 7% churn / 14-month Starter lifetime, and the input was still not corrected. The $920 correction only came at t30, and the 5% / 20-month input was never stated.

faults.quote: Earlier you said "$1,880" for the loss on each customer who moved from Pro to Starter.
faults.why: The acknowledgment and the tail say the same thing twice in one turn.

faults.quote: Putting it all together, what would you recommend to the CEO, and what's the biggest risk to it?
faults.why: The interview moved to the recommendation without ever running the brainstorm stage, and the case ended without it.

faults.quote: We're almost out of time — what would you tell the CEO, and what's the biggest risk to it?
faults.why: The candidate had just given a recommendation, risk and next steps in t31.

faults.quote: We're almost out of time — what would you tell the CEO, and what's the biggest risk to it?
faults.why: The candidate's $60 uplift of '$150–180k a month' (case: +$0.24M, built on the uncorrected 14-month lifetime) was never probed or corrected. The case closed with this wrong figure inside the recommendation.
